name: Summoner Wars 2E - Gate Placement Guide
one_line: Strategy article on where to place your Gate, a permanent structure that opens new summon points anywhere adjacent to it
take_what: a Gate is a '0-cost event that sticks around' - place it and it permanently extends your legal-summon frontier away from your home base; 'knight's move' Gate placement (2 tiles diagonal-ish) yields 4 new summon spaces compactly, letting units appear where the opponent can't prepare
constraint: none - mechanism only, no IP risk to mirror the pattern

name: Summoner Wars 2E - Beginner's Guide
one_line: New-player strategy primer covering unit tempo, gate blocking, and the 3-action turn economy
take_what: explicit design principle: 'most units, especially commons, have their biggest impact on the turn they are summoned' - the game is built so holding cards is a trap, not a strategy, because fresh units get an immediate move+attack; also 'if your unit is adjacent to an opponent's gate, they cannot summon to that spot' making gates contestable board objects, not just static resources

name: Summoner Wars 2E - First Thoughts review (The Solo Meeple)
one_line: Player review/postmortem of first games, noting event-card timing tricks and the payoff of forward summoner pushes
take_what: reviewer initially played it safe/defensive and found the game punishing - 'defensive play initially seemed more prudent' but forward Summoner+Gate pushes into enemy territory won; also event cards that force a unit to move after attacking read as 'getting an extra move' - a small burst effect that reads as huge because it breaks the expected action economy

name: Summoner Wars - UltraBoardGames rules (Master Set / 1E)
one_line: Full rules writeup: 6-phase turn (Draw, Summon, Events, Move, Attack, Build Magic), Magic Pile as deck-as-resource, hard action caps
take_what: hard per-turn caps - move up to 3 units (2 spaces each), attack with up to 3 units - deliberately prevent 'flooding the board and grinding'; separately, Magic is paid by discarding cards straight off your own draw deck (Magic Pile), so every point of mana literally thins your future hand - your deck is simultaneously your card supply and your mana pool
constraint: the deck-as-mana coupling is a strong lever for Limen's 'decks feel thin' problem - it makes a 20-card deck feel weightier because every summon has an opportunity cost against future draws

name: BGG search summary - Summoner Wars 2E design overview & event-card combo tech
one_line: BGG thread cataloging 1E-to-2E rule changes: magic became a cleaner track, dice/combat streamlined, and 'silly strategies' (attacking own units for magic, turtling) were removed
take_what: 2nd edition specifically patched degenerate stalling loops - players discovered you could attack your own units to farm magic points, or turtle indefinitely behind walls; the designers closed both exploits rather than balancing around them, which is the direct anti-pattern lesson for Limen's 'players build up in their own corners' problem - identify and specifically close the turtle-payoff loop rather than adding a soft nudge
constraint: page returned 403 on direct fetch, information drawn from search-result summary of the thread; verify directly before citing numbers

name: Summoner Wars event-card summon tricks (Summoning Surge, Forced Summon, Mirage)
one_line: How-to-play breakdown covering the Event Phase and cards that let you summon mid-event, ambushing from unexpected board positions
take_what: a distinct 'Play Events' phase sits between Summon and Movement in the turn order; certain event cards let you summon a SECOND unit during this phase from a wall/gate the opponent didn't expect, creating a one-two ambush inside a single turn - the trick is entirely about phase-order exploitation, not raw card power
constraint: Limen's 3 spell 'rites' could gain a similar phase-order trick: a rite that lets you place a second tile after your normal placement, contingent on already having placed near the rift

name: Summoner Wars 2E - Dunky Stack / gate-protection tech (referenced in Beginner's Guide)
one_line: Community-named tactic: stack units directly behind your own Gate so the Gate itself blocks incoming ranged attacks
take_what: a placed structure (Gate) doubles as both a summon-anchor AND line-of-sight cover for units stacked behind it - one placed object serves two mechanical roles simultaneously, rewarding spatial reasoning about a single tile rather than adding new tile types
constraint: Limen's towers (stack own tiles 3-high, +1/tier) could borrow this: let a tower ALSO block line-of-sight/targeting for tiles behind it across the rift, giving towers a second reason to exist besides raw influence stacking

name: Colby Dauch interview - Shut Up & Sit Down / Plaid Hat Games
one_line: Interview with Summoner Wars designer Colby Dauch on Plaid Hat's founding and design philosophy
take_what: little mechanic-specific content surfaced - Dauch's stated approach is 'release only great things' over frequent iteration, and Summoner Wars was rejected by Hasbro as 'something an in-house designer could replicate,' i.e. its core loop reads as simple/replicable on the surface but the depth is in phase-order and spatial interactions covered in the other rows
constraint: low signal for concrete mechanics; keep for context only, do not treat as a primary source of numbers
